## Evidence (reproduced 2026-07-26 against the installed 2026.7.26 build)

Running `pm deps <id> --add <other> --kind blocked_by` — a plausible wrong guess, because `--add` is the annotation idiom everywhere else — produces this recovery hint:

```
Next steps:
  - --add is a valid option on: comments, notes, learnings. If you meant one of
    those, run that command instead.
```

The enumeration is presented as exhaustive and is not. Probing every candidate command directly:

| command | accepts `--add` |
|---|---|
| comments | yes |
| notes | yes |
| learnings | yes |
| files | **yes — omitted** |
| docs | **yes — omitted** |
| test | **yes — omitted** |
| deps | no (read-only surface) |

Six commands accept `--add`; the hint names three. The three it drops include `pm files --add`, which was the command actually wanted in the reproducing session. The hint did not merely fail to help — it actively asserted a closed set that excluded the right answer, and an agent that trusts structured recovery output (which this repository asks agents to trust) is steered away from the fix.

The same truncation is observable on an unrelated flag: `pm graph predecessors <id> --depth 8` reports `--depth is a valid option on: context, get, plan`, again capped at three.

## Root cause

`src/cli/commander-usage.ts:429-446`, `findOtherCommandsForFlag`:

```ts
return commands
  .filter((command) => command !== normalizedCurrent)
  .slice(0, 3);
```

Two independent defects in four lines.

1. **Silent truncation.** `.slice(0, 3)` drops the tail with no `+N more` marker and no `truncated` field in the recovery bundle, so neither a human nor a parser can distinguish "these three" from "three of six". Every other bounded collection in this CLI carries a truncation signal — `pm list` emits `truncated`, `pm validate` emits `*_truncated`, `pm graph` emits `truncated`. This surface does not.

2. **Arbitrary retention order.** The retained three are whichever the cross-command flag index happened to enumerate first; nothing ranks candidates by proximity to the attempted command, by shared noun family, or by argument-shape compatibility. When the cap does bind, which three survive is an accident of index construction order, so the most probable intent has no better chance of surviving than the least probable one.

The consumer at `src/cli/error-guidance.ts:1232` renders the list into prose that reads as complete: `"${optionName} is a valid option on: ${otherCommands.join(", ")}. If you meant one of those, run that command instead."` The phrase "one of those" is a closed-world claim the producer cannot honour.

## Why this matters more than its size suggests

Recovery bundles are the output an agent reads at exactly the moment it is already wrong. A wrong-but-confident hint costs a retry cycle plus the tokens of a second failure, and the failure mode is silent: the agent does not learn that the list was partial. This is the specific class of defect that `pm-cha95z` argues about in aggregate (diagnostics are the most-read output with the least discipline) — this item is one concrete, fixable instance with a four-line root cause.

## Deliverable

- The cross-command list is ranked before it is capped, so the cap keeps the best candidates rather than the first ones. Ranking uses signals already available: command-family adjacency (annotation family, query family, lifecycle family), and whether the attempted argument shape is accepted by the candidate.
- When the cap binds, the rendered prose and the structured recovery bundle both say so, using this repository's existing truncation vocabulary rather than a new one.
- The structured bundle carries the full candidate list under a bounded ceiling even when the prose is capped, because a parser has no reason to be limited to what fits a sentence.
- A regression test asserts the reproducing case: `--add` on a command that does not accept it enumerates `files`, `docs`, and `test` among the candidates or declares truncation.

## Relationship to neighbours

- `pm-8nyc` (closed) built this cross-command suggestion feature. This is a defect in the shipped result, not a request for the feature; recorded as `discovered_from` so the escape is attributable.
- `pm-rtn5h6` requires every escaped defect to land a gate that would have caught it. The gate here is the assertion that any capped enumeration in a recovery bundle declares its truncation — a rule, not a single case.
- `pm-gdi7` covers unknown-option errors suggesting valid flags *for the attempted command*. This item is the orthogonal axis: which *other commands* accept the flag. Neither subsumes the other.
- `pm-cha95z` owns the diagnostic-output budget as a whole; this instance argues that a budget without a truncation contract produces confidently wrong output rather than merely short output.
Unknown-option recovery names three of six commands that accept the flag, capped silently and in arbitrary order, so the hint excludes the right answer while reading as exhaustive

pm deps --add reports '--add is a valid option on: comments, notes, learnings' while files, docs and test also accept it; findOtherCommandsForFlag slices to 3 with no truncation marker and no relevance ranking, and error-guidance renders it as a closed set ('if you meant one of those'). Duplicate check 2026-07-26: searched unknown-option/recovery/cross-command/flag-suggestion items across all statuses; pm-8nyc (closed) built this feature, pm-gdi7 covers same-command flag suggestions, pm-cha95z covers diagnostic budget in aggregate. No open item covers the cross-command enumeration being silently partial.

The cross-command candidate list is relevance-ranked before any cap is applied, so a binding cap retains the best candidates rather than the first-enumerated ones; when the cap binds, both the rendered prose and the structured recovery bundle declare truncation using this repository's existing truncation vocabulary; the structured bundle carries the full candidate set under its own bounded ceiling independent of what fits the prose sentence; a regression test asserts that --add on a non-accepting command enumerates files, docs and test among candidates or declares truncation; the closed-world phrasing 'if you meant one of those' is only emitted when the set is genuinely complete
A recovery hint never asserts a closed candidate set it did not compute
Agents that trust structured recovery output stop being steered away from the correct command; one retry cycle saved per occurrence
Reproduced live on the shipped 2026.7.26 build while probing the annotation family; the hint dropped pm files --add, which was the command actually needed

value.text: Reproduced at HEAD 2026-07-31 on a different flag than the original report. `pm context --limit 10 --summary` recovery bundle states "--summary is a valid option on: graph, deps, health" — three commands. A direct sweep of --help across nineteen read commands finds four that accept --summary: deps, graph, health and contracts. The hint reads as exhaustive and omits one, on a flag whose whole purpose is reducing output.
